Dmitri Mendeleev is a chemist. The synthetic element mendelevium is named in his honor.
What is the atomic number of Livermorium?
Livermorium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lv and atomic number 116.
What is the atomic number of Polonium?
Polonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Po and atomic number 84.
In what year did Alan Turing die?
Alan Turing: Alan Mathison Turing (23 June 1912 – 7 June 1954) was an English mathematician, computer scientist, logician, cryptanalyst, philosopher and theoretical biologist.
In what year was Magnesium discovered?
Magnesium is a chemical element; it has symbol Mg and atomic number 12.
Adenosine: Pfizer. Adenosine (symbol A) is an organic compound that occurs widely in nature in the form of diverse derivatives.
Which country is HAL Tejas from?
HAL Tejas: India. The aircraft made its first flight in 2001 and entered into service with the IAF in 2015.
Who is credited with discovering Grus?
Grus (constellation): Petrus Plancius. Grus (or colloquially) is a constellation in the southern sky.
Who is credited with discovering Reynolds number?
Reynolds number: Sir George Stokes, 1st Baronet. At low Reynolds numbers, flows tend to be dominated by laminar (sheet-like) flow, while at high Reynolds numbers, flows tend to be turbulent.
Who is credited with discovering Ceres?
Ceres (dwarf planet): Giuseppe Piazzi. Ceres is a dwarf planet in the main asteroid belt between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
This localized collection of pus builds up within body tissue, usually from bacterial infection, causing redness, pain, warmth, and swelling. What is it?
Abscess is a collection of pus that has built up within the tissue of the body, usually caused by bacterial infection.
First described by Othniel C. Marsh in 1877, this late Jurassic theropod's name means 'different lizard,' a nod to its unusually lightweight vertebrae — what dinosaur is it?
Allosaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived 155 to 143 million years ago during the late Jurassic period (latest Oxfordian to latest Tithonian ages).

Named in 1835 from the Greek for 'flower' and 'dark blue,' these pH-shifting pigments paint blueberries, black rice, and some autumn leaves anything from red to purple to nearly black — what are they?

Anthocyanin (from Ancient Greek (nthos) 'flower' and / (kuneos/kuanos) 'dark blue'), also called anthocyans, are water-soluble vacuolar pigments that, depending on their pH, may appear red, pink, purple, blue, or black.
First described in 1740, this flowering-plant family rivals only the orchid family in sheer number of species, with over 32,000 recognized today — what family is it?
Asteraceae is a large family of flowering plants that consists of over 32,000 known species in over 1,900 genera within the order Asterales.

This fluid-dynamics rule holds that a fluid's pressure drops as its speed increases; the Swiss physicist credited with it published the idea in 1738, though Leonhard Euler derived the actual equation — what's it called?
Bernoulli's principle is a key concept in fluid dynamics that relates pressure, speed and height.
This incurable, always-fatal disease of cattle causes abnormal behavior and trouble walking, with symptoms that may take four to five years to appear after infection — what is this disorder called?
Bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), commonly known as mad cow disease, is an incurable and always fatal neurodegenerative disease of cattle.

One species in this genus of flowering shrubs, native to southern China and Indochina, has its leaves processed into the world's tea, while thousands of ornamental cultivars exist for the garden. Name the genus?
Camellia is a genus of flowering plants in the family Theaceae.
Taken by mouth with effects lasting about a day, this second-generation antihistamine treats hay fever, hives, and dermatitis with less drowsiness than older allergy medications — what is it?
Cetirizine is a second-generation peripherally selective antihistamine used to treat allergic rhinitis (hay fever), dermatitis, urticaria (hives), and runny nose.
Its Latin genus name literally means three-leaf, and this herbaceous legume, native to Europe, now grows worldwide in around 300 species — what plant is it?
Clover are plants of the genus Trifolium (from Latin tres 'three' and folium 'leaf').

This cosmopolitan bird family includes crows, ravens, magpies, and jays, and its roughly 135 species are known for remarkable intelligence, including self-awareness demonstrated in mirror tests — what's the family?
Corvidae is a cosmopolitan family of oscine passerine birds that contains the crows, ravens, rooks, magpies, jackdaws, jays, treepies, choughs, and nutcrackers.

First patented in Germany in 1920, then independently synthesized by an American chemist in 1932 and marketed in German-speaking Europe as Permonid for its fast onset and short duration, what is this semi-synthetic opioid?
Desomorphine (or in some formulations known as Krokodil) is a semi-synthetic opioid commercialized by Roche, with powerful, fast-acting effects, such as sedation and analgesia.
Along with the platypus, this quill-covered Australian and New Guinean mammal is one of only two living egg-laying mammal groups, and its young are adorably called puggles — what is it?
Echidna are quill-covered monotremes (egg-laying mammals) belonging to the family Tachyglossidae, living in Australia and New Guinea.
This taxonomic family groups hedgehogs of Eurasia and Africa together with the furrier moonrats of Southeast Asia, and takes its name from the Latin for 'hedgehog' — what family is it?
Erinaceidae (from Latin erinaceus, "hedgehog") is a family in the order Eulipotyphla, consisting of the hedgehogs and moonrats.
This field of study, related to economics and business administration, is typically divided into personal, corporate, and public branches. What field is it?
Finance refers to monetary resources as well as the discipline that studies such resources, with related concepts such as money, currency, assets and liabilities.
Testimony at Joaquín 'El Chapo' Guzmán's 2018 trial revealed suitcases stuffed with $3 million in bribes paid to this former Mexican security chief — who is he?
Genaro García Luna (born 10 July 1968) is a Mexican former government official and convicted drug trafficker.
This Italian-American motorsport boss ran a Formula One team for seven years before becoming CEO and owner of a MotoGP outfit — who is he?
Guenther Steiner (born 7 April 1965) is an Italian and American motorsport engineer and former team manager.
This seasonal state of low body temperature, slow breathing, and reduced metabolism helps some animals pass through winter months — what is it?
Hibernation is a state of minimal activity and metabolic reduction entered by some animal species.
First appearing in the fossil record in Egypt some 37 million years ago, this order of small African herbivores once rivaled odd-toed ungulates in size and diversity — which order?
Hyracoidea is a taxonomic order of mammals.

This English independent scientist invented the electron capture detector, was first to spot CFCs spread through the atmosphere, and proposed that the Earth behaves as one self-regulating system. Who was he?
James Lovelock (26 July 1919 - 26 July 2022) was an English independent scientist, environmentalist and futurist.
This Soviet-designed naval helicopter has spawned variants for assault transport, export, and civilian use, and still flies today from Russia to India -- which aircraft?

Kamov Ka-27 (NATO reporting name 'Helix') is a military helicopter developed for the Soviet Navy, and as of 2024 is in service in various countries including Russia, Ukraine, Vietnam, China, South Korea, and India.

A hybrid of the citron and the bitter orange believed to have originated in northeastern India around the 1st millennium BC, this small evergreen citrus tree bears a tart yellow fruit used worldwide — name the fruit?
Lemon (Citrus limon) is a species of small evergreen tree in the Citrus genus of the flowering plant family Rutaceae.
Dubbed the 'Queen of QVC' for her long-running shopping show and holding over 120 patents, this American entrepreneur is also an investor on the reality series Shark Tank — who is she?
Lori Greiner is an American television personality and entrepreneur.

This Milanese thinker was the first woman to write a mathematics handbook and the first appointed a mathematics professor — though she spent her final decades on theology and serving the poor. Who was she?
Maria Gaetana Agnesi (16 May 1718 - 9 January 1799) was a Milanese mathematician, philosopher, theologian, and humanitarian.

Named from Greek words meaning 'small head,' this congenital condition involves a smaller-than-normal head and can affect brain development, intellectual ability, and motor function — which disorder is it?
Microcephaly (from Neo-Latin microcephalia, from Ancient Greek mikrs "small" and kephal "head") is a medical condition involving a smaller-than-normal head.
Named for the strong odor males emit during rut to attract mates, this thick-coated Arctic hoofed mammal is called 'the bearded one' in Inuktitut — what's the species?
Muskox (Ovibos moschatus) is a hoofed mammal of the family Bovidae.
First isolated by Scottish physician Daniel Rutherford, which group-15 nonmetal with atomic number 7 is the most abundant species in Earth's atmosphere?
Nitrogen is a chemical element; it has symbol N and atomic number 7.
The heaviest living bird, this flightless African species can sprint at 70 km/h and lays the largest eggs of any land animal on Earth — what bird is it?

A Chinese singer famous for annual appearances on a widely watched Lunar New Year television gala, she has served as her country's First Lady since 2012 as the wife of its paramount leader — who is she?

Peng Liyuan (pinyin: Png Lyun; born 20 November 1962) is a Chinese singer who has served as the First Lady of China since 2012, as the wife of Xi Jinping, the General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party and paramount leader of China.
The sole genus in its plant subfamily, this evergreen conifer bears needle-like leaves in bunches of two to five and carries its seeds on woody cones — name the tree?
Pine is any conifer in the genus Pinus of the family Pinaceae.

This oral glucocorticoid medication suppresses the immune system and reduces inflammation in conditions like asthma and COPD, though long-term use risks side effects such as cataracts and bone loss — what's the drug called?
Prednisone is a glucocorticoid medication mostly used to suppress the immune system and decrease inflammation in conditions such as asthma, COPD, and rheumatologic diseases.
Element 88 on the periodic table, this silvery-white alkaline earth metal turns black when exposed to air and glows via radioluminescence as it radioactively decays — which element?
Radium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ra and atomic number 88.

Usually hidden below the soil surface but sometimes growing aerial or aerating instead, these plant organs anchor a plant while drawing in the water and nutrients it needs to grow taller and faster — name them?
Root are the organs of a plant that are modified to provide anchorage for the plant and take in water and nutrients into the plant body, which allows plants to grow taller and faster.

Native to the North Pacific coasts, this marine mammal is the heaviest member of the weasel family yet one of the smallest marine mammals, insulated by the densest fur coat in the animal kingdom — what is it?
Sea otter (Enhydra lutris) is a marine mammal native to the coasts of the northern and eastern North Pacific Ocean.
Commonly but inaccurately nicknamed for a big cat it wasn't closely related to, this extinct genus of saber-toothed predator roamed the Americas until as recently as 8,200 years ago — which genus?
Smilodon is a genus of extinct felids. It is one of the best-known saber-toothed predators and prehistoric mammals.

Starting with fever and flu-like symptoms before the skin blisters and peels into painful raw patches, this severe drug-triggered skin reaction sits on the same disease spectrum as toxic epidermal necrolysis, only less severe — which condition?
Stevens–Johnson syndrome (SJS) is a type of severe skin reaction.

Tucked beneath the lateral fissure of the brain and named for its position near the head's temples, this region handles language comprehension, memory, and emotion — which part of the cerebral cortex?
Temporal lobe is one of the four major lobes of the cerebral cortex in the brain of mammals.
These brightly colored Neotropical birds are known for their oversized, vividly patterned bills, and their chicks hatch completely naked with no down feathers at all — what bird is it?
Toucan are Neotropical birds in the family Ramphastidae.
This member of the herpesvirus family causes chickenpox in children and, upon reactivation later in life, shingles in adults — what is it called?
Varicella zoster virus (VZV), also known as human herpesvirus 3 (HHV-3, HHV3), is one of nine known herpes viruses that can infect humans.
This broad category of limbless, tube-bodied animals ranges from microscopic creatures to a marine species measured at nearly 58 meters long — the longest animal on Earth — what are they called?
Worm are many different distantly related bilateral animals that typically have a long cylindrical tube-like body, no limbs, and usually no eyes.
This mucolytic drug is the go-to antidote for acetaminophen overdose, working by boosting glutathione to neutralize the drug's toxic byproducts — what is it?
Acetylcysteine: Medication used to treat overdose of paracetamol.
Twice President of the Swiss Confederation, this Social Democratic politician left the Federal Council in 2023 to become Secretary General of the Council of Europe — who is he?
Alain Berset: Swiss Federal Councillor from 2012 to 2023.
Nicknamed the boto for its rosy pink hue (especially in males), this South American toothed whale is the largest species of its kind found in a freshwater habitat — what is it?
Amazon river dolphin: Species of toothed whale. The position of the Araguaian river dolphin (I. araguaiaensis) within the clade is still unclear.
This American anthropologist studied women's weaving and blacksmithing work in Indonesia and later designed microcredit programs to fight rural poverty — who was she?
This pigmented ring of skin around the nipple contains sebaceous glands as well as the openings of the milk ducts — what's it called?
Areola: Pigmented area on the breast around the nipple.
This genus of early African hominins, which lived during the Pliocene and Early Pleistocene, is considered ancestral to the genus that includes modern humans — which genus?
Australopithecus: Genus of hominin ancestral to modern humans. The genera Homo (which includes modern humans), Paranthropus, and Kenyanthropus evolved from some Australopithecus species.
With more than 2,000 species and petals but no sepals, this flowering plant genus originated in Africa and is popular as an ornamental houseplant in cooler climates — which genus?
Begonia: Genus of perennial flowering plants.
This medium-sized antelope of India and Nepal sports corkscrew horns up to 30 inches long and a striking two-tone coat, with white around the eyes set against black face stripes — which animal?
Blackbuck: Antelope native to India and Nepal. The blackbuck (Antilope cervicapra), also known as the Indian antelope, is a medium-sized antelope native to India and Nepal.
Nicknamed 'murderer's thumb' or 'stubbed thumb,' this genetic trait gives about 2% of people a short, rounded thumb linked to the HOXD13 gene — what is it?
Brachydactyly type D: Abnormal shortening of the distal part of the thumb.
Alongside HTML and JavaScript, which style sheet language handles the layout, colors, and fonts of a webpage — separating presentation from content?
CSS: Style sheet language. CSS is a cornerstone technology of the World Wide Web, alongside HTML and JavaScript.

This group of heart-muscle diseases includes the 'broken heart syndrome' type and can lead to irregular heartbeats, fainting, or even sudden cardiac death — what's the general term for this condition?
Cardiomyopathy: Disease of the heart muscle. In dilated cardiomyopathy the ventricles enlarge and weaken.
Also known as an ischemic stroke, this necrotic brain condition is the second-leading cause of death worldwide and a leading cause of physical disability — what is it?
Cerebral infarction: Stroke resulting from lack of blood flow.
This class of jawed fish — including sharks, rays, skates, and ghost-like chimaeras — has skeletons made entirely of cartilage rather than bone — what is it called?
Chondrichthyes: Class of jawed cartilaginous fish. Chondrichthyes are aquatic vertebrates with paired fins, paired nares, placoid scales, and conus arteriosus in the heart.
Nicknamed the 'palm thief,' this giant terrestrial arthropod can weigh over 9 pounds, making it the largest land-dwelling arthropod alive today — what is it?
Thanks to a variation in the gene OR6A2, some people taste this herb — called cilantro in the US — as fresh and citrusy while others swear it tastes like soap. What is it?
Coriander: Annual herb. Coriander, or Coriandrum sativum, is an annual herb in the family Apiaceae.
Its Greek name literally means 'boat beard,' describing how its hairy spikelets project from boat-shaped sheaths — better known by a common name evoking a citrus scent, what is this grass genus?
First patented in Germany in 1920 and later synthesized by an American chemist in 1932, this semi-synthetic opioid is roughly ten times more potent than morphine — what is it called?
Desomorphine: Semi-synthetic opioid, morphine analogue. It was first discovered and patented in Germany by a German team working for Knoll in 1920 but was not generally recognized.
Despite its common names, this evergreen conifer isn't a true member of the pine, spruce, or hemlock genera, yet stands as the tallest species in its own family — what is it?
Douglas fir: Species of tree. It is native to western North America and is also known as Douglas-fir, Douglas spruce, Oregon pine, and Columbian pine.

A subfield of physics and electrical engineering, this discipline uses transistors, diodes, and integrated circuits to control and amplify current — and to convert AC to DC or analog to digital — what is it?

Electronics: Branch of physics and electrical engineering. The semiconductor industry is one of the global economy's largest and most profitable industries, with annual revenues exceeding $481 billion in 2018.
About 60 to 70 percent as sweet as table sugar yet virtually calorie-free, this sugar alcohol is fermented from corn and was commercially pioneered by Japanese companies in the 1990s — what is it?
Erythritol: Sugar alcohol that is used as a sweetener.
Sporting a dark facial mask and famous for a seriously foul-smelling territorial secretion, this stocky mustelid ranges across the continent and Morocco's Rif mountains — which species is it?
Belonging to the genus Abies, these evergreen conifers have cones that stand upright like candles and disintegrate at maturity, and some varieties serve as Christmas trees — which conifer genus?
Fir: Genus of coniferous trees. The genus is most closely related to Keteleeria, a small genus confined to eastern Asia.
Often bonded to glucose to form sucrose, this simple sugar is found in honey, fruit, and most root vegetables — which sugar?
Fructose: Simple ketonic monosaccharide found in many plants.

Among the longest of all living crocodilians, this fish-eater wields a slender snout lined with 110 interlocking teeth, and the males sport a bulbous, pot-shaped bump on the tip that gives the animal its name. What is it?
Gharial: Crocodilian native to the Indian subcontinent.
This branch of discrete mathematics studies structures made of vertices connected by edges, modeling pairwise relationships between objects — what field is it?

Graph theory: Area of discrete mathematics. In mathematics and computer science, graph theory is the study of graphs, which are mathematical structures used to model pairwise relations between objects.

This British aviation entrepreneur held three Guinness World Records after visiting the South Pole, the Challenger Deep, and space, then died in 2023 aboard the submersible that imploded near the Titanic wreck — who was he?
Also known as the cane spider or giant crab spider, this huntsman species native to the tropics has spread to subtropical regions worldwide — what is it?
Heteropoda venatoria: Species of spider. It is native to the tropical regions of the world, and it is present in some subtropical areas as an introduced species.
Marketed as Hydrodiuril, this medication treats high blood pressure and fluid retention by blocking sodium and chloride reabsorption in the kidneys' distal tubules — what drug is it?

Hydrochlorothiazide: Diuretic medication. Hydrochlorothiazide, sold under the brand name Hydrodiuril among others, is a diuretic medication used to treat hypertension and swelling due to fluid build-up.
First described to Europeans in 1812, this reddish-brown African antelope's males sport lyre-shaped horns up to three feet long — which animal?
Impala: Species of antelope found in Africa.
A Harvard chemistry professor who studied chlorophyll and helped develop poison gas in WWI, he later became Harvard's president and the first U.S. ambassador to West Germany — who is he?
Nicknamed "Marvellous Merchiston," this 16th-century Scottish laird discovered logarithms and popularized the decimal point — who was this mathematical wizard?
Deafened by childhood illness and rerouted from competitive diving, she became a Hollywood stunt pioneer and earned the title 'the fastest woman in the world.' Who was she?
Kitty O'Neil: American stuntwoman and racer (1946–2018)
Named after the Latin for 'ghosts of the dead' for their large eyes and nocturnal habits, these primates are found only on Madagascar — what are they?
Lemur: Clade of primates endemic to the island of Madagascar.
This four-engine American turboprop can land on dirt strips and unprepared runways, then moonlight as a gunship, a flying firefighter, or a weather scout — which versatile workhorse is it?
Lockheed C-130 Hercules: American military transport aircraft.
Nicknamed for a Native American tribe, this mulberry-family tree produces a bumpy, orange-like fruit that oozes sticky white latex and is rarely eaten by animals — what's its scientific name?
Maclura pomifera: Plant species in the fig family.
This American psychologist completed every requirement for a Harvard Ph.D. in 1895 but was denied the degree because of her gender — who was she?
Mary Whiton Calkins: American philosopher and psychologist. In 1903, Calkins was the twelfth in a listing of fifty psychologists with the most merit, chosen by her peers.

From a Greek word meaning 'change,' this term covers the enzyme-driven reactions that turn food into usable energy and building blocks while excreting waste — letting organisms grow and reproduce. What is it?
Metabolism: Set of chemical reactions in organisms.

Prized for their fur and related to weasels and otters, these semiaquatic carnivores have established wild populations in Britain and Denmark after farm escapes and animal-rights releases — what are they?
Mink: Mammal in the family Mustelidae.
In this autoimmune disease the immune system attacks myelin, the insulation around nerve cells, so the central nervous system can't transmit signals properly — what condition?
Multiple sclerosis: Disease that damages the myelin sheaths around nerves.
Also called roundworms, these mostly free-living animals have a tubular digestive tract with openings at both ends and are grouped with arthropods in the clade Ecdysozoa — what are they?

Introduced in 2001 and originally developed under the name Tier II+, which remotely piloted, high-altitude surveillance aircraft supports the US Air Force with long-endurance radar and infrared sensors?
Northrop Grumman RQ-4 Global Hawk: Unmanned surveillance aircraft. It was initially designed by Ryan Aeronautical (now part of Northrop Grumman), and known as Tier II+ during development.
First domesticated in China's Yangtze River basin more than 8,000 years ago, this grass species is the world's most widely cultivated rice — which species?
Oryza sativa: Species of plant. Oryza sativa belongs to the genus Oryza and the BOP clade in the grass family Poaceae.
Defined as the distance at which one astronomical unit subtends an angle of one arcsecond, this unit equals about 3.26 light-years — which unit?
Parsec: Unit of length in astronomy.
Smaller than 3 millimetres and caused by leaking capillaries, these tiny red or purple skin spots can be forensically significant when found around the eyes or neck — what are they called?
Petechia: Small red or purple blemish on the skin, eyes, etc. due to rupture of capillaries.

Cultivated for its edible nuts since prehistoric times and native to the Mediterranean and the Levant, this pine species has earned the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit — which species?
Pinus pinea: Species of pine tree. Pinus pinea, the Italian stone pine or Mediterranean stone pine, is a tree from the pine family, Pinaceae.
Stockpiled for radiation emergencies, this oral compound floods and shields the thyroid gland — and also treats hyperthyroidism and the skin infection sporotrichosis. Which compound is it?

Harvested from Plantago seeds mainly grown in northern India, this dietary fiber relieves both constipation and mild diarrhea, and can modestly lower cholesterol and blood pressure with regular use. What is it?
Psyllium: Plant used as a dietary fiber.
This genus of muroid rodents gives its scientific name to the common rat, though not every animal called a rat actually belongs to it — which genus?
Sold under the brand name Rituxan, this monoclonal antibody treats non-Hodgkin lymphoma, rheumatoid arthritis and several other autoimmune conditions via slow IV infusion — what is it?
Named after a 19th-century American veterinary surgeon, this genus of rod-shaped, flagella-covered bacteria includes over 2,650 serotypes divided among just two species — what is it?
Salmonella: Genus of bacteria. Salmonella is a genus of rod-shaped, (bacillus) Gram-negative bacteria of the family Enterobacteriaceae.
This class of central nervous system depressant increases GABA activity to calm irritability and anxiety, distinct from drugs used mainly to induce sleep — what is it?
Sedative: Drug that reduces excitement without inducing sleep.
This structural framework supporting an animal's body can take the form of a rigid outer shell, an internal bony frame, or simply fluid pressure inside the body. What is it?
Skeleton: Part of the body that forms the supporting structure.

Encased by the vertebral column and running from the brainstem down to about the first lumbar vertebra, this hollow, fluid-filled structure forms the other half of the central nervous system alongside the brain — what is it?
Spinal cord: Part of the vertebral column in animals.
Made by chlorinating ordinary table sugar and roughly 600 times sweeter than it, what is this sugar substitute also known by the E number E955?
This daisy-family weed's yellow flowers give way to fluffy silver-tufted seed heads nicknamed 'clocks' or 'blowballs,' whose seeds scatter on the wind — which plant, better known by its common name?
Taraxacum officinale: Flowering plant species known as dandelion.
This French aerospace engineer flew to the International Space Station twice, first as a 2016 European Space Agency flight engineer and again in 2021 aboard a SpaceX Crew Dragon — who is he?
Thomas Pesquet: French aerospace engineer, pilot, and astronaut.
Inside a ribosome, this cellular process reads messenger RNA three nucleotides at a time to build a chain of amino acids into protein — what is it called?
Translation (biology): Cellular process of protein synthesis. Translation is the process in biological cells in which proteins are produced using RNA molecules as templates.
RIKEN has been trying to synthesize this hypothetical element 119 since 2018 — the lightest element not yet made and the first of the eighth period. What is it?
Ununennium: Theoretical chemical element with atomic number 119 (Uue)
Running a boutique called Sex with partner Malcolm McLaren, this English designer helped bring punk fashion into the mainstream and shaped the look of the Sex Pistols — who is she?
A short-legged, stubby-tailed marsupial native to Australia, this burrowing animal can weigh up to 35 kilograms and survives in an isolated pocket of central Queensland — which creature?
Wombat: Species of marsupial native to Australia.
Protactinium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for protactinium is Pa. Protactinium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pa and atomic number 91.

In what year was Eva Mendes born?

Patrick Swayze: Patrick Wayne Swayze ( SWAY-zee; August 18, 1952 – September 14, 2009) was an American actor, singer-songwriter and dancer.

Paul Reubens: Reubens developed his Pee-wee character at the Groundlings.

Truman Capote: Capote had a troubled childhood caused by his parents' divorce, a long absence from his mother, and multiple moves.

Audrey Hepburn: Audrey Kathleen Hepburn (née Ruston; 4 May 1929 – 20 January 1993) was a British actress and humanitarian.

In what year was Trainspotting first released?
Trainspotting (film): Based on the 1993 novel by Irvine Welsh, the film was released in the United Kingdom on 23 February 1996.

The Smurfs: The Smurfs wear Phrygian caps, which came to represent freedom during the modern era.
